You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 16, has left education or training and been registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for less than 20 weeks

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation

  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by accessing the official assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started with your Child Benefit eligibility assessment, I need to understand your situation.

**First, let me ask you about the child (or children) you're inquiring about:**

1. **Do you have a child or children you're responsible for?** If yes, could you tell me:
   - How many children?
   - What are their names (or you can use Child 1, Child 2, etc. if you prefer)?
   - How old is each child?

This information will help me guide you through the eligibility requirements accurately.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I have one child. His name is Alex and he's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So you have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16, there are additional criteria we need to check. Let me navigate to the relevant section.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now, for Alex at age 16, Child Benefit eligibility depends on his education or training status. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following situations?**

1. **Currently enrolled in approved education or training** (such as school, college, or an approved training program)

2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)

3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex recently left school. He's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. So Alex recently left school and is working with the careers service. Let me check the extension eligibility rules for young people who have recently left education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! This is important. There's a special 20-week extension period for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education and registered with certain services.

Let me ask you a few specific questions:

1. **When exactly did Alex leave school?** (How many weeks ago?)

2. **Which careers service did he register with?** You mentioned it's the "local careers service" - is this:
   - A government careers service
   - Connexions (a youth support service in some areas)
   - Or another type of service?

3. **When did he register with this service?**

This 20-week extension can cover Alex while he's registered with a qualifying careers service and deciding on his next steps, but we need to confirm the timing and that it's an approved service.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been a couple of months since he left school. He registered with the government careers service pretty much right after leaving. I think it was the same week, actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information! So Alex left school a couple of months ago (which is within the 20-week extension period) and registered with the government careers service right away in the same week.

This is good news - Alex appears to qualify for the 20-week extension period because he:
- Left approved education recently (within the last 20 weeks)
- Registered with a qualifying service (government careers service)

Let me move to the next check to continue the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

For Child Benefit purposes, young people aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week (and aren't in approved education/training) are not eligible.

What's Alex's current work situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all right now. He's just focusing on working with the careers service to figure out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's helpful to know. Since Alex isn't working, he meets this requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits claimed in his own name

(This doesn't include Child Benefit that you might be receiving for him - I'm asking if Alex himself is claiming any benefits in his own name)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't claiming any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Next question about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship program?**

If yes, I'll need to know:
- What type of apprenticeship it is
- Where it's based (England, Scotland, or Wales)

If no, that's fine too - just let me know.

(Note: Different apprenticeship types have different rules depending on the region)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just working with the careers service right now to figure out what he wants to do.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, thank you for clarifying! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, we can move forward. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask about your residency situation, as this is a requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, I'll need to check if you meet one of the special circumstances (such as having settled or pre-settled status, being a Crown servant abroad, etc.)

What's your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Living in the UK meets the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now about your relationship with Alex and your responsibility for him:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards his care - this can include food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** for Alex under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex lives with you, you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Another parent or guardian
- A former partner
- Anyone else

If someone else is claiming, only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child at a time. What's the situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following best describes where Alex is currently living?**

1. **In hospital** (staying in hospital for medical treatment)
2. **In care** (placed in local authority care)
3. **Fostered** (living with foster parents)
4. **Normal living** (living at home with you normally)

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living at home with me normally.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council contributing financially to Alex's living costs or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me get the final outcome for you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex! ✓**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for your 16-year-old son Alex.

### **Why You're Eligible:**

Alex qualifies under the **special 20-week extension period** for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education. Specifically:

- ✓ Alex is 16 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- ✓ He left school a couple of months ago (within the 20-week extension period)
- ✓ He registered with the government careers service right away (a qualifying service)
- ✓ He's not working 24+ hours per week
- ✓ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✓ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✓ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✓ Alex lives at home with you
- ✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✓ The local council is not paying towards his accommodation

### **Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

### **Important Information:**

- **Payment frequency**: Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)
- **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: Be aware that if you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through your tax return
- **Extension period**: Remember that this 20-week extension will expire either at the end of the 20 weeks or when Alex turns 18, whichever comes sooner. If Alex enrolls in approved education or training during this time, his eligibility could continue beyond the 20 weeks

**For more information and to apply:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?
